description: Developing an Early Warning System to Prevent Heat Illness in North Carolina is published by U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit. The case describes developing heat-illness warning information using health and weather evidence. Its stated coverage is North Carolina, United States. Further dates and resolution are unknown unless specified by the provider. The application account is available online as an HTML page; underlying model files and operational data were not inspected. The account is free to read; the terms and cost of its underlying tools and data are separate. A reuse licence is not stated in the inspected metadata. The government case account was read; underlying forecast models and health microdata were not obtained. For simulation, it can inform designing or comparing infrastructure simulation cases; the documented application is evidence of context, not a ready-to-run model; this is a reviewer assessment of potential use. Related record model-jemss provides a comparison in the same service area; technical compatibility was not tested.

outcomes: The provider reports that user feedback led the tool to use heat index rather than maximum temperature. Its 2017 evaluation found use of the tool and materials in decision support; a reduction in illness was not established by this account.
